recipes.name: Basil Pecan Pesto
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Combine basil, pecans, olive oil, Parmesan cheese, garlic, salt, and black pepper in the bowl of a food processor; pulse until blended.

raw_recipe.headline: Basil Pecan Pesto
raw_recipe.description: In this basil pecan pesto recipe, pecans replace the typical pine nuts, creating a fresh and delicious change-up to a familiar Ligurian pasta sauce.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! I used toasted pecans. My pesto has a brownish color with flecks of the bright green basil. I used some on pasta and froze some for later use. Great recipe - I will be using it again! Update - I made this again with raw pecans. This time I got the lovely green color we all come to expect from a good pesto. I love what the sweetness of the pecans do for this pesto. Truly delicious!

this is now my family's favorite recipe. We use it as spread on sandwiches, we add tofutti sour cream for a cream pesto pasta sauce, we use it on pizza, we add it to baked chicken, we grill with it on burgers...their most favorite is pulled chicken and mozzarella in a pan toasted wrap. Quick, easy, and fabulous!
Great twist on pesto. Loved the pecans. Like others I roasted them. Once I finished blending I added roughly chopped sun dried tomatoes and olives for a Puttanesca style pesto.

Seemed a bit flat, so I added some lemon juice and a couple of tablespoons of white wine vinegar. I'd also recommend either reducing the amount of nuts, or adding additional oil or maybe some white wine, because as written this came out way too thick. I did replace about half of the pecans with walnuts because that's what I had on hand, but I don't think that was the reason for either problem. I also missed that subtle "turpentine" flavor of the pine nuts, but maybe a splash of retsina would solve that?

Thanks for the idea of using pecans! I will make this again. FYI, I toasted the pecans in the microwave first to add more depth of flavor. (Melt 2 tsp to 1 tablespoon butter or margarine in medium bowl; toss in 1 1/2 cup nuts. Spread nuts out evenly on large microwave safe plate and toast 1 minute at a time, stirring at those intervals until a nice toasty smell develops ~2-5 minutes. Check often as microwaves differ of course. Also, if the nuts seem too crowded, toast in more than one batch.)

Toasting the pecans before adding to the food processor really brings out the pecan flavor - worth the extra time. I am now sadly allergic to pine nuts, and this recipe satisfy that craving for fresh basil pesto. This pesto makes an excellent spread over toast - I like to use jalapeno cheddar bread from my local grocer. The best, I have to say, is making a grilled cheese sandwich using mozzarella and/or havarti, adding the pesto spead to the insides of both slices with cheese in the middle and grill slowly, allowing the pesto to warm up and the cheese to melt. An open face egg over easy sandwich is also delicious!

Love this! I cut back to 1 cup of pecans (not toasted) and it seems just right to me. I put everything into the food processor except the oil, chopped it all up, and then added the oil through the tube as the processor was running. Made a double batch last weekend and will probably do that again this weekend (storing in the freezer). Food Network has a page of 50 things to do with pesto which has some great ideas. Thanks for sharing your recipe; I never liked those pine nuts!

Really good.....I veganized it and made it satvic (mode of goodness). I used lemon zest and nutritional yeast instead of parmesan and I used 1/4 t. hing (asafoetida powder...gives a garlicky flavor). I also lightly toasted the pecans and used less olive oil. Thank you for the inspiration.

I have a bumper crop of basil this year so I wanted to turn some of it into pesto. Pine nuts are so expensive so when I saw this recipe called for pecans I figured this was the one to try. It is delicious! I added 1/4 tsp of fresh lemon juice to it to help it keep its beautiful color.

I loved this recipe! Kept close to the measurements (recipes like this don't have to be precise). I used a really good parm from one of the Italian markets in my hood. I added a pinch of red pepper flakes to give it a little kick.
This is a great basic pesto recipe. I put 1 cup of cheese instead 1.5. I drizzle a little EVOO on top and freeze in 1 cup containers. Use it quite a bit with shrimp and pasta

I, too, toasted my pecans. Really beautiful flavor. I added sautéed cremini mushrooms and cherry tomatoes. I may try finishing with a bit of lemon to brighten the sautéed veggies, but the pesto on its own definitely is delicious!
I have pecan trees and basil growing like crazy on my Tower Garden so I'm always looking for easy and delicious ideas! I added a splash lemon juice to brighten it up too.
I love pine nuts but they’re so expensive. I had some raw pecans that I toasted first and OMG I love this stuff!!!
Very tasty. Usually use pine nuts, but pecans from now on.
Amazing way to use your end of season harvest of basil! I froze these in quart size bags and use 1/4 to 1/2 of a bag directly into my recipes. Amazing!!!
I made 2/3 of the recipe and used more garlic, just because. If tastes great.
Wonderful recipe - just added lemon zest and a little juice for brightness. Will definitely make always!
My sons are lactose intolerant so I made it without the cheese. Used roasted pecans instead… loved it!
I like more parmesan, so I added an extra 1/4 cup and also 2 more garlic cloves! It's aromatic and a lively green! A wonderful way to use my extra healthy crop of basil this summer! Thank you!
